correctness.rationale: For all integers h,m>=2, open-neighborhood direct utility inequalities reduce algebraically to r_i-r_j>=2 and r_i+r_j=2R-(h-1)m. A decreasing integer potential bounds improving swaps. For h=3, the three pair-event sizes are A_m-B_m, each intersection has size J_m and the triple intersection is empty, yielding the exact count. The lattice local CLT for Bin(2m,1/2)+2Bin(m,1/2), with variance 3m/2, plus two-constraint O(m^-1) bounds gives the asymptotic. Standalone explicit-utility enumerations verify 42,816 colorings and 1,468,544 opposite-type oriented swap possibilities at tested sizes; finite tests are not used as proof of the universal theorem.

value.rationale: The explicit hyperplane criterion identifies precisely where mutual relocation is possible in an infinite family of dense three-community networks; the exact binomial equilibrium count and inverse-square-root instability law quantify an unexpected concentration of stable placements. This resolves a natural graph-and-preference counting question, not just a routine numerical invariant. General almost-regular convergence is not claimed as novel.
